![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/2264aa2a4f3d33b04190608ab638604dbe09dfd278035b2b764aa3d85d947624.png)

Greta is flying a kite $K.$ The kite is  $150\,\text{in}$ above the ground and moving horizontally towards Greta at a speed of $10\,\text{in/s}.$ Find, in radians per second as a function of $\theta ,$ the rate at which the angle $\theta $ between the kite string and the horizontal is increasing.
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/430d9bccfa7d9063ef3be511b894f23227fc248eb6afde9a25dc78546dde32aa.png)

In the figure, $y$ is the kite's height, and $x$ is the horizontal distance between Greta and the kite. The quantity $y=150$ inches does not change with time because the kite height remains the same.

We wish to calculate $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$
To do this, let's start by setting up a relation between $x$ and $y.$ Relative to the angle $\theta ,$ the sides $x$ and $y$ are the adjacent and opposite, respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{y}{x} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{150}{x} \\ x & =150\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(150\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =(-150{csc}^{2}⁡\theta )\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given information, we have $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-10.$ Substituting this into the above, we reach

$$
\begin{aligned}-10 & =(-150{csc}^{2}⁡\theta )\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{1}{15} & =({csc}^{2}⁡\theta )\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate at which the angle between the kite string and the horizontal is increasing is $\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{15}$ radians per second.
